Your subscriptions and your settings, kept somewhere you choose. All off until you turn something on \u2014 the only part of Whisper that can send your data anywhere.

Two things here are worth keeping: the subscription list you spent a long time building, and the settings you arranged to suit you. Both exist only on this phone. Choose somewhere to keep a copy and Whisper will write it there once a day.

Nothing on this screen happens unless you ask for it.\n\nWhisper has no server and no account of its own, so this is the only part of the app that can send your data anywhere. Everything here is off until you turn it on: no folder is chosen, and Android\u2019s own backup hands over nothing. Turn on what suits you \u2014 and nothing else will leave this phone.

Everything here is off. Nothing is leaving this phone.

When you set up a new phone next to this one. A direct copy \u2014 no server involved.
Your feeds and reading history are kept in your Google account. Convenient, but it does leave the phone.

Android can carry apps to a new phone by itself. Whisper hands over nothing unless you switch it on here, and the two are asked separately because they are different things. Your sign-in tokens are never included either way \u2014 they cannot survive the trip, and restoring them would stop the app starting.
Sources are added without removing anything you already have. Settings replace what is on this phone, which is why the two are asked separately.

A backup is two files. Your sources and their categories go into an OPML file, which any other reader can open; your settings go into a JSON file beside it. Neither contains articles, and neither records what you have read.
Optional. Keep your subscriptions and read state in step across devices.

Whisper works completely without an account — everything stays on this phone. Connecting one keeps your subscriptions and what you have read in step with another device, through a service you choose or run yourself.
That does not look like a web address. It should look like https://example.com/api/greader.php

That address was reached but nothing answered on it. Check the server is running, and that the port is right.

Nothing here is guessed. These are counts of what you pressed, what reached your screen, and what you opened — and the effect each has on how prominently a source appears. An article you opened counts for a great deal more than one you scrolled past. None of it leaves your phone.

Some launchers let another app fill the page to the left of the home screen — the slot Google Discover uses on a Pixel. Whisper can be that page. This is a bonus rather than a requirement: the app works exactly the same without it.

Turn on Ignore feed whitelist. Lawnchair keeps a fixed list of apps allowed to be the feed, and Whisper is not on it yet.
Go to Home screen settings → Feed provider and choose Whisper.
Without this, the page appears but tapping an article does nothing. On a sideloaded build the switch is greyed out until you allow it: Settings → Apps → Whisper → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings.

Nothing is fetched in the clear — Whisper already asks for https even when a feed is stored as http. What is still wrong is the address itself: it is what the sources list shows and what an OPML export hands to the next reader. Each one is checked before anything is changed.

resources.string: Nothing yet. Once a week Whisper looks for two things: other sites that the articles you opened keep linking to, and publications that sit beside your own sources in its bundled collections \u2014 so following two papers from one country can turn up a third.\n\nNeither asks anything of anyone. The collections ship with the app, and the links are counted in articles already on your phone.
How much you read, and when
Your busiest sources, by articles that reached your screen.
Articles that reached your screen, over the last %1$d days.
When you read, summed across the whole month.
%1$d articles seen and %2$d opened over %3$d days.
There is not enough reading yet to draw your own, so the charts below show made-up figures to give you an idea of the shape. They will be replaced by yours once you have read a little more.
Whisper has only counted opened articles since a recent update, so days before that show none even if you read them. This will fill in from here.

Worked out on your phone. Whisper keeps a running count of how many articles reached your screen and when \u2014 numbers only, no titles and no addresses \u2014 because the articles themselves are tidied away after a week and these charts would otherwise forget their own past. Nothing leaves the device, and the source breakdown reflects what you have been reading lately rather than the full 30 days.
Hundreds of feeds by topic and country, bundled with the app

A directory that ships with Whisper, so nothing is fetched and no one is told what you are looking for. Open a collection to see what is in it \u2014 everything starts ticked, and nothing is added until you say so.
